risks: Two seeds may be insufficient to observe a reliable crossover point in the accuracy-gap curves
The non-augmented model may not overfit within 30 epochs on Fashion-MNISTs 60K training set requiring even longer runs
Effect sizes may be below 0.5% throughout making any conclusions highly uncertain
title: Augmentation benefit direction in 5-epoch underfitting regime

impact.why: Answers a practically important question about when augmentation is worth applying under compute-constrained training.

novelty.why: None of the prior work specifically investigates whether geometric augmentation is neutral or harmful at very short training runs (~5 epochs) versus beneficial at longer runs on Fashion-MNIST with a small CNN; the closest works (e.g., 'State-of-the-Art Results with the Fashion-MNIST Dataset' and 'Multi-Class Image Classification on Fashion-MNIST') use augmentation with longer training schedules (20–100 epochs) without studying the epoch-regime dependency of augmentation benefit.

feasibility.why: Directly extends the core study protocol with only additional epoch-count variants on the same infrastructure.

testability.why: Accuracy at each epoch count is a fully determinate numerical outcome with a clear comparison criterion.

approach: Run the core 5-epoch protocol for both conditions with seeds 42 and 123, then extend training to 10, 20, and 30 epochs using the same seeds and architecture. Record test accuracy and training/validation loss at each endpoint. Plot the accuracy gap (augmented minus non-augmented) as a function of epoch count to determine whether 5 epochs falls in a regime where augmentation is neutral or harmful and identify the epoch at which consistent benefits first appear.
question: Does basic geometric augmentation improve or degrade test accuracy of a small CNN trained for only approximately 5 epochs on Fashion-MNIST, where underfitting rather than overfitting is likely to dominate?
why_open: Studies demonstrating augmentation benefits such as (Çetiner et al. 2023) and (Imam et al. 2026) train models for 50–200 epochs on CIFAR-10 where overfitting dominates, making their results inapplicable to the 5-epoch underfitting regime. (Lin et al. 2023) explicitly shows augmentation can degrade performance when underfitting occurs but does not quantify this effect for Fashion-MNIST or short training budgets. (Guo 2024) shows that even LeNet-5 achieves only 90% validation accuracy on Fashion-MNIST at similar training lengths, suggesting small CNNs operate in a capacity-limited regime where augmentation may introduce harmful noise rather than beneficial regularisation.
hypothesis: At 5 epochs of training a small CNN on Fashion-MNIST has insufficient capacity utilisation for augmentation to provide a regularisation benefit, resulting in equal or lower test accuracy for the augmented condition, with the benefit emerging only after 15–25 epochs when the non-augmented model begins overfitting.
data_needed: Fashion-MNIST via torchvision (60K train, 10K test); no additional data required
